LESSON: TWO-PART HARMONY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Foundations of Music and Dance
Topic 1.5: Two-Part Harmony
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 11

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Two-Part Harmony, part of Foundations of Music and Dance in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How is a second part added to an existing melody? 2. How can intervals be utilized in improvising a second part to a melody?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Two-Part Harmony together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner speaks clearly and effectively when describing harmonic

intervals.

● Creativity and imagination: The learner comes up with new musical ideas when composing the second part to a

4-bar melody.

● Digital Literacy: The learner records the 2-part music using a digital device with appropriate assistive

technology.

18

Values:
● Respect: The learner recognizes the input of every member of the team as they participate in group activities

involving sounding harmonic intervals.

● Integrity: The learner uses own music ideas without plagiarism.

● Unity: The learner collaborates with others in sounding harmonic intervals in group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Cyber security: The learner uses digital devices with assistive technology responsibly as they record the 2-part

music.

● Safety and security: The learner takes precaution while interacting with digital devices.

● Self-esteem: The learner gains confidence as they compose music.

Suggested Learning Resources

Digital devices with appropriate assistive technology, Sheet music in appropriate print and in music braille

notation, Braille equipment and materials, Textbooks in appropriate print and in braille format, Manuscripts books

in appropriate print, melodic instrument, piano keyboard, print and braille Flash cards- of two-part harmony

melodies, Music Braille Code, 2015

Audio/visual recordings of songs, Pitching device, Song book in appropriate print and in braille, Internet

connectivity.

Suggested Key Skills Assessed

● Guidelines for creating two-part harmony.

● Composing a second part to a 4-bar melody in a major key.

Core competencies to be developed:


  -  Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups as they interact with the music notation software.


  -  Critical thinking: The learner manipulates several functions in music notation software to key and edit created

melodies using music notation software.


  -  Problem solving: The learner uses digital devices with appropriate assistive technology to edit and play back

music they already created.


  -  Creativity and imagination: The learner comes up with new ideas while using music notation software to

compose music.


  -  Learning to learn: The learner uses demos as a guide to write music using music notation software.


  -  Digital literacy: The learner uses music notation software to key in created melodies.

Values:


  -  Respect: The learner recognises the input of others when appraising each other’s music.


  -  Responsibility: The learner uses the digital devices with appropriate assistive technology for the intended

purpose.


  -  Unity: The learner works with others in groups to key in music in music notation software.


  -  Integrity: The learner uses digital devices with appropriate assistive technology observing ethical and legal

standards.


  -  Social justice: The learner critiques each other’s work without exception.

21

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCI
s) :


  -  Peer Education: The learner actively contributes to group decisions when keying in and editing music.


  -  Social cohesion: The learner actively participates in group activities as they manipulate the functions of the

music notation software.


  -  Safety and security: The learner takes precaution when using digital devices with appropriate assistive

technology powered by electricity.

Suggested Learning Resources

Digital devices with appropriate assistive technology, Sheet music in appropriate print and in music braille

notation, Braille equipment and materials, Textbooks in appropriate print and in braille format, Manuscripts books

in appropriate print, Internet connectivity.

Suggested Key Skills Assessed


  -  Identifying notation software in music writing.


  -  Navigating selected music notation software.


  -  Transcribe music using a music notation software.


  -  Save music files for storage.
